text:
Lucas Raymond is the steadiest thing in Detroit right now, which is a strange compliment in a season the Red Wings spent waiting out the Dylan Larkin saga. He has 22 points in 23 games, 10 of them on the power play, while playing almost 20 minutes a night against the other team's best. Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 90th percentile last season, and that hasn't changed.

Nothing about his scoring looks borrowed. His goals sit within one of what his chances deserved, and his last ten games produced 10 points against an expected 9.9. Our range for his scoring rate runs from 2.5 to 3.3 points per 60, all of it well above the league's 2.1.

The worry is the team around him: Detroit lost eight of those ten games. What to watch is who he's passing to once Larkin's minutes are redistributed. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.7 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 87th percentile among forwards, and a setup man needs someone to finish.
